author: brand
comment: The section motivates cost and access well, but it does not end in a precise research question or hypothesis. Add an explicit question such as whether a low-cost differential-drive, 3D-printed platform can satisfy a defined subset of SSL performance constraints under a specified control architecture. Or Consider focusing on performance in particular scenarios. It is ok if we deviate from these scenarios later but we need to have one in mind here.

author: brand
comment: You introduce PID and MPC, but the methodology later implements only PID. Remove MPC from the framing unless the proposal will genuinely compare controllers.

author: brand
comment: The literature review does not distinguish clearly between educational low-cost platforms and competition-grade SSL robots. Build that distinction explicitly because it is central to the proposed contribution.

author: brand
comment: We need a problem statement and research questions section with appropriate content included.Right now the proposal says, in effect, "I will build a robot and test it." That is not enough for research. The reader needs to know exactly what you are trying to prove. Otherwise, even if the robot works, it will be unclear what lesson the results are meant to support.State one primary research question and, if needed, one or two secondary questions. For example: can a low-cost differential-drive platform built from 3D-printed parts and low-cost electronics satisfy a defined subset of SSL motion and control requirements? Then map each benchmark directly to that question.

comment: The protocol does not explain calibration, synchronization, or logging. I am not saying it is needed but it is worth thinking about the needed procedures for timestamp alignment, clock source selection, trial reset conditions, battery-state control, and floor-surface consistency.
